chokepointsNote: preCrisisBaselineMedian on every row is computed over one fixed window (baselineWindowStart to baselineWindowEnd) anchored to the Hormuz crisis. For hormuz that window is a genuine pre-crisis baseline. For bab-el-mandeb, suez and cape it is not: those routes were already carrying diverted Red Sea traffic within that window, so preCrisisBaselineMedian for those rows reads as wartime volume, not a peacetime figure.

bullets: BREAKING: IRGC Quds Force commander Qaani called on Saudi Arabia to lift its blockade on Yemen, per Iranian state media, widening the diplomatic front around Hormuz-adjacent waterways.
US forces redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled two non-compliant ships enforcing the naval blockade against Iran, per CENTCOM as reported by ANI and IBTimes.
Crisis Pressure remains in the extreme band, easing over 24 hours; PortWatch recorded 15 transits on 2026-07-19 against a pre-crisis baseline of 88 per day.
dailyBrief.summary: The Strait of Hormuz continues to operate at a fraction of its pre-crisis throughput: PortWatch's most recently published day (2026-07-19) recorded 15 transits against the pre-crisis baseline of 88 per day. A separate methodology tracking port arrivals across Hormuz-area ports on both the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman sides recorded 435 arrivals in the most recent 24-hour window, while AIS data at the time of writing (11:52 UTC) showed 413 vessels anchored or stopped in the region. Neither figure should be read as equivalent to the other or to a full-transit count. Brent was quoted at $96.78 at 11:52 UTC, unchanged from the 2026-07-25 brief; no fresh print has emerged from the feed, and the 24-hour reported move stands at -0.90%. The Hormuz Index places Crisis Pressure in the extreme band, easing over 24 hours, with physical transit deviation as the top contributor; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, also easing, with Polymarket escalation contracts as the dominant driver. The divergence between extreme current pressure and a high (rather than extreme) forward signal suggests markets are pricing in some probability of diplomatic relief without yet discounting it fully. Iranian state media reports constructive Iran-Oman talks on safe navigation, though Iranian officials simultaneously stated no change in transit conditions, and those claims are not independently confirmed. The most consequential political signal in the past six hours is IRGC Quds Force commander Qaani's call, per Iranian state media, for Saudi Arabia to lift its blockade on Yemen, a move that would formally link the Hormuz crisis to the Red Sea front and complicate any near-term de-escalation track.

pipelineBypass.notes: Saudi Aramco's East-West Pipeline carries Arabian Light from Abqaiq to Yanbu on the Red Sea, the single largest non-Hormuz route for Gulf crude.

pipelineBypass.name: ADCOP (Habshan-Fujairah)
pipelineBypass.notes: ADNOC's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline lifts UAE crude past the Strait of Hormuz to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, where it loads on tankers transiting the open Indian Ocean.

pipelineBypass.name: Goreh-Jask Pipeline
pipelineBypass.notes: Iran's pipeline from the southwest oilfields to Jask on the Gulf of Oman bypasses the Strait, but throughput remains a fraction of nameplate capacity.
